snippet.title: When Kirsten Dunst Did Her Own Stunts🕸️
snippet.description:
In Sam Raimi's 2002 film Spider-Man, Kirsten Dunst took on more physical responsibility than audiences might expect from a supporting role at the time, performing several of her own stunts rather than relying on a stunt double throughout production. Among these was a notable balcony sequence, filmed practically on set without the use of a CGI double to replace her for the more physically demanding moments. Doing her own stunts allowed for more natural movement and continuity between close-up shots and wider action sequences, something that can be harder to achieve seamlessly when cutting between an actor and a double. The decision reflected a broader commitment to grounded, practical filmmaking that helped define the tone of Raimi's original Spider-Man trilogy. Dunst's willingness to perform these sequences herself added a layer of authenticity to scenes that might otherwise have felt visibly stitched together.
